column1: # ci-splits.tsv: packages CI's test shards run as more than one entry (scripts/ci_shard.sh, ci.yml's test step).
# <package>\t<-run regex>\t[<label>]. A row is one #entry: the label (default A) names the entry, <package>#<label>,
# which runs `go test -run <regex>`. Rows sharing a package are its parts; the package's own entry runs every test
# minus those regexes (and TestHeads). The balancer places each entry by its weight in ci-pkg-times.tsv; every entry
# is a go test call of its own, so a package with N rows runs as N regex calls plus one whole-minus-regex call.
# engine/rules (11-20 two-way, 11-27 four-way): the fuzz-world, quiet-proof, clone-fidelity and elimination sweeps
# are ~40% of its CPU and the bare package the rest. The three rows below split both halves into four ~equal parts:
# A = quiet-proof chunks 0-3 + every Test[A-C]* (which holds the whole clone-fidelity family); B = quiet-proof
# chunks 4-7 + kernel-world games 0-1 and game 2's four shards + Test[D-GI-J]* (H is left out so TestHeads stays only on the Golden step);
# C = quiet-proof chunks 8-11 + kernel-world games 3-4 + every Test[L-P]*/Test[R]* (L holds the elimination sweep).
# The package's own entry is the fourth part: kernel-world game 5's two shards + GameSweep + quiet-proof chunks
# 12-15 + every Test[KQ-S-Z]*. Keep this row group's four regexes mutually disjoint: each top-level test must match
# exactly one of them or fall to the whole entry. The four groups share no writer (every fixed-path writer in the
# package is env-gated off in CI; see scripts/ci-pkg-times.tsv's engine/rules weights).
github.com/adams-shaun/gorge/engine/rules
github.com/adams-shaun/gorge/engine/rules
github.com/adams-shaun/gorge/engine/rules
# testkit/conformance (11-21, median 239 s; CPU-bound JSON wire simulation, already parallel inside its tests): the
# ManaBrew wire tests (~72 s of serial games) apart from the native-wire game sets.
github.com/adams-shaun/gorge/testkit/conformance
# dirac/kgen (11-27, batch 45936102895: 182 s, one call, the shard's floor; 1219 tests). Its all-corpus work is lumpy
# by first letter, so the split names the five table tests and the two census tests instead. Every sync.Once build
# group (tables, pool, census, corpus acceptance) stays whole in one half, so no once-only build is paid twice: the
# four table tests share one build and TestTableBuildDeterministic's second build stays beside them. The one fixed
# path both halves may write, .cards/kgen/ALL.txt via corpusAllList, is written whole and renamed from a unique temp
# file with identical bytes, so concurrent writers cannot corrupt it. ci.yml runs kgen's halves with -count=1.
github.com/adams-shaun/gorge/dirac/kgen
# bots/azmcts (11-27, batch 45936102895: 176 s, one call; 179 tests). The S block is 43 tests and its heaviest family,
# so A-J plus the Search family (~half the search work) makes the two halves 89/90 tests with the heavy helpers split
# 46/43. No per-process build is shared between azmcts tests; the golden/net writers are env-gated off in CI.
github.com/adams-shaun/gorge/bots/azmcts
# engine/effects (11-27, batch 45936102895: 167 s, one call; 1861 tests). The letters split 924/937, and the only
# shared per-process build (the compiled-vs-textual filter oracle fixture, ~12 s of parallel chunks) stays with its
# eight chunk tests in the #A half; the other half carries 17 more corpus-walking tests. Only env-gated regen paths
# write, so the halves never share a file.
github.com/adams-shaun/gorge/engine/effects
